dedupe_keys.name: miami dade county digital twin with a synthetic population to pre test hurricane evacuation messages

description: This case study builds a digital twin of Miami-Dade County, Florida, populated with a synthetic population of AI agents whose decisions follow behavioural theories (the Extended Parallel Process Model and the Theory of Planned Behavior), and uses it to test hurricane evacuation messages. The authors, researchers at MITRE, developed a Message Assessment Framework and published the work in an open-access journal article. Agents received fear-only, efficacy-only, norm-only, combined fear and efficacy, combined fear, efficacy and norm, or neutral control messages. Coverage is one county. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: this is a proof of concept with simulated agents, so effect sizes are not validated against real evacuation behaviour. The study found that theory-based messages encouraged evacuation more than the control, that combined fear and efficacy messages worked best (odds ratio 15.45), and that adding social norm cues gave no clear extra benefit. Simulation uses: an example of agent-based digital twins for testing emergency communication before hurricanes and for adding warning response to evacuation models. Related records: the Florida statewide regional evacuation study surge zones (data-florida-statewide-regional-evacuation-study-surge-zones) define the evacuation areas such messages target.
